system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:39:57, WS-MLOPEZ-01 recorded a network logon for omar.haddad from WS-OHADDAD-01. About two minutes later, PowerShell ran under omar.haddad with the command to execute \\FILE-HD-01\IT\Deploy-Patches.ps1; this matches the documented IT patching method.

The PowerShell process launched wusa to install a Windows 11 update, while the proxy recorded a Windows Update download of about 38.8 MB. These events support a patching explanation for the reported PowerShell activity.
The PowerShell and wusa processes ended shortly afterward.

WS-MLOPEZ-01 requested Kerberos tickets for ben.carter and the WS-BCARTER-01 computer account; WS-BCARTER-01 then recorded a network logon for ben.carter from WS-MLOPEZ-01. Later, DC-HD-01 recorded a network logon for maria.lopez from WS-BCARTER-01. The supplied records do not explain this cross-workstation authentication sequence.

The proxy recorded connections to clients4.google.com with a GoogleDriveFS user agent and to desktop.dropbox.com with a DropboxUpdate user agent. The inventory does not list Google Drive or Dropbox as approved services, but these records alone do not establish file sharing or data transfer.
WS-MLOPEZ-01 made an SMB connection to FILE-HD-01, where the recorded network logon was ANONYMOUS LOGON. The available records do not show what share or files, if any, were accessed.

known_telemetry_limitations: Winsec and Sysmon collection was unavailable on WS-LPARK-01 from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, so activity on that host during the outage cannot be assessed.
The supplied SMB records show connections and a logon but not share-level operations or accessed file names.
The supplied Google Drive and Dropbox proxy records show CONNECT metadata and byte counts, not the contents or purpose of the traffic.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish that the PowerShell execution was malicious; its account, command, and subsequent update activity are consistent with the documented patching practice.
The evidence does not establish whether the cross-workstation authentication sequence was authorized or why it occurred.
The evidence does not establish that Google Drive or Dropbox transferred organizational files or data.
The evidence does not establish that the anonymous SMB session accessed any FILE-HD-01 share or data.
The contents, integrity, and authorization status of Deploy-Patches.ps1 and the installed update are not established by these records.
additional_evidence_needed: Review WS-OHADDAD-01 remote-execution and administrative activity, plus the approved patch deployment record for WS-MLOPEZ-01.
Verify the contents, signature or hash, and provenance of \\FILE-HD-01\IT\Deploy-Patches.ps1 and the installed update package.
Review WS-BCARTER-01 authentication and SMB/share audit records to explain the cross-workstation logons.
Check endpoint software inventory and relevant proxy or endpoint file-operation records to determine whether Google Drive or Dropbox was installed or used for file transfer.
Recover or review WS-LPARK-01 logs for the collection-outage period if activity on that host may be relevant.
